_readme: SAIRNlaw deadline engine -- New Jersey holiday calendar. Loaded through
add_holidays alongside sql/sairnlaw_deadline_seed_newjersey.json.
== ONE YEAR ONLY, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE SOURCE, NOT A SHORTCUT =====
Every other jurisdiction here carries 2026-2031; North Carolina carries
2026-2027. NEW JERSEY CARRIES 2026 ALONE. Read why before trying to extend it.
New Jersey's legal holidays for the courts are fixed by ORDER OF THE SUPREME
COURT OF NEW JERSEY, issued one court year at a time, and a New Jersey court
year runs 1 JULY TO 30 JUNE. So calendar year 2026 is assembled from TWO
orders -- January to June 2026 from the 2025-2026 order, July to December 2026
from the 2026-2027 order -- and calendar 2027 cannot be completed at all,
because the July-December half of it belongs to a 2027-2028 order that has not
been issued. Both source orders were read on 2026-08-25.
A HALF-KNOWN 2027 WAS DELIBERATELY NOT LOADED. The engine refuses on a missing
YEAR, not on a missing day, so a 2027 calendar holding only the January-June
holidays would look complete and would silently under-report every holiday in
the second half of the year. Refusing all of 2027 is the honest behaviour.
Load it when the 2027-2028 order is published, and re-run this every July.
DO NOT DERIVE THE MISSING YEARS FROM N.J.S.A. 36:1-1. See the seed readme --
that statute is the wrong source, and it is wrong in the LATE direction.
== THE ORDER DISTINGUISHES LEGAL HOLIDAYS FROM RECESSES, AND SO DOES THIS ==
Each order marks some days "Legal Holiday (Emergent Matters Only)" and others
"Court Recess" or "Statewide Judicial College", also emergent matters only.
ONLY THE DAYS THE ORDER ITSELF CALLS LEGAL HOLIDAYS ARE ENCODED. R. 1:3-1
rolls a last day off "a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday" -- it does not
mention recesses -- so encoding the recess days would roll deadlines LATER
than the rule provides, which is the direction that misses a filing.
Excluded on that basis for 2026: the Statewide Judicial College on Monday to
Wednesday 23-25 November 2026, and the Court Recess from Monday 28 December
2026 through Thursday 31 December 2026. The courts are largely shut on those
days and a practitioner will feel the difference; the rule still does not make
them legal holidays. A deadline computed across them is EARLY, never late.
== TWO ENTRIES THAT LOOK LIKE MISTAKES AND ARE NOT ========================
COLUMBUS DAY IS A NEW JERSEY LEGAL HOLIDAY. Monday 12 October 2026 is in the
order by name. North Carolina and Washington both EXCLUDE Columbus Day -- North
Carolina because its courts do not close, Washington because RCW 1.16.050(7)
says its recognized days "may not be considered legal holidays for any
purpose". Three states, three answers, and New Jersey is the one that counts
it. Do not carry another state's treatment across.
GENERAL ELECTION DAY IS A LEGAL HOLIDAY, EVERY YEAR. Tuesday 3 November 2026
is in the order, and so was Tuesday 4 November 2025 in the previous one --
New Jersey elects its General Assembly annually, so unlike Illinois, Indiana,
West Virginia and Georgia, where statewide election days fall in even years
only, New Jersey's recurs every year. That is a reason not to generate this
calendar from an even/odd rule.
JUNETEENTH IS THE THIRD FRIDAY IN JUNE, NOT 19 JUNE. N.J.S.A. 36:1-1(a) says
"the third Friday in June, Juneteenth Day", and the orders follow it: 19 June
2026 and 18 June 2027. In 2026 the third Friday happens to fall on the 19th,
which will make a naive 19-June rule look correct for exactly this year and
then fail. Every other state seeded that observes Juneteenth -- Washington --
fixes it on the calendar date.
GOOD FRIDAY MOVES and is a legal holiday here: 3 April 2026, 26 March 2027.
== NO WEEKEND-SHIFT RULE IS APPLIED, BECAUSE THE ORDER ALREADY DID IT =======
The order states observed dates directly. Independence Day 2026 appears as
FRIDAY 3 JULY 2026 because 4 July 2026 is a Saturday; nothing here computes
that shift, it is read off the order. This is the opposite of West Virginia and
Washington, where a statute states the shift and the calendar applies it.

authority.citation: Orders of the Supreme Court of New Jersey scheduling legal holidays and court recesses for the 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 court years, as applied to time computation by N.J. Ct. R. 1:3-1
authority.note: Read 2026-08-25 from two Orders of the Supreme Court of New Jersey: the order for the court year 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026 supplies January to June 2026, and the order for 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 supplies July to December 2026. New Jersey fixes its court legal holidays by ORDER, one court year at a time, and a court year runs July to June -- so a calendar year is assembled from two orders and 2027 cannot be completed until the 2027-2028 order issues. ONLY DAYS THE ORDERS THEMSELVES LABEL "Legal Holiday" ARE ENCODED. The same orders separately designate a Statewide Judicial College (23-25 November 2026) and a Court Recess (28-31 December 2026), both "Emergent Matters Only"; R. 1:3-1 rolls off a "legal holiday" and says nothing about recesses, so encoding those would push deadlines LATE. NOT DERIVED AND NOT DERIVABLE: Columbus Day IS a New Jersey legal holiday (North Carolina and Washington both exclude it); general election day is a legal holiday EVERY year, not in even years only, because New Jersey elects its General Assembly annually; Juneteenth is "the third Friday in June" per N.J.S.A. 36:1-1(a), NOT 19 June, and 2026 is the year that coincidence hides the difference; and Good Friday moves. The observed-date shift is already applied by the order (3 July 2026 for Independence Day) and is not computed here.
